Army social media policy: Driscoll directive
Army orders mass shutdown of official social media accounts

status_summary: A Defense Department chief of staff memo of 2025-01-24 paused posting to official accounts for ten days, and an email of 2025-02-03 lifted the pause while directing organizations to use social media primarily to communicate their mission, showcase lethality, promote meritocracy and readiness and support recruiting, according to DefenseScoop. An Army Secretary memo dated 2026-06-30 and released 2026-07-08 limits official accounts to listed headquarters, commands, formations and installations and orders unauthorized unit accounts deactivated within 30 days, with exceptions for mission-critical needs; personal accounts are not covered. No policy limiting official use solely to recruiting or disciplining personnel for engaging critics was found.

timeline.event: A Defense Department email rescinded the ten-day pause on official social media posting and directed organizations to use social media primarily to communicate their mission, showcase lethality, promote meritocracy and readiness, and support recruiting.

The Army Secretary signed the memo Optimizing Digital Media, limiting official Army social media to listed organizations and ordering unauthorized unit accounts deactivated within 30 days (publicly released 2026-07-08).

title: Limit official social media to recruiting and discipline engagement with critics
uncertainties: Neither the January 2025 memo, the February 2025 email nor the June 2026 Army memo was read directly; all rest on DefenseScoop and Military Times. The 2025 email lists recruiting as one of several primary purposes, which differs from the Mandate's solely-for-recruitment test. The Army consolidation is framed by the Army as reducing operational risk, not as a restriction to recruiting. Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force and Space Force policies and any Defense Department instruction changes were not examined, and no disciplinary policy on engaging civilian critics was found in a limited search.
